China's heavy-lift pad — Long March 5 to Tianhe, Chang'e 5/6, Tianwen-1, and the lunar return programme

Long March 5 / 5B pad at Wenchang Space Launch Site on Hainan Island. LC-101 is dedicated to Long March 5 / 5B. First flight of Long March 5 from LC-101: November 3, 2016. Sister pad LC-201 (Long March 7/8) had its debut in June 2016. Wenchang's southern latitude (19.6°N) adds free orbital velocity vs the older inland sites — that's how China can fly Long March 5B with the 25-tonne LEO payload class. Lifted the Tianhe core module (April 2021), Chang'e 5 (November 2020), Chang'e 6 (May 2024), Tianwen-1 (July 2020). Coordinates from CNSA + Xichang Satellite Launch Center public records.

Built in 2014, operational from 2016, on Hainan Island at 19.6°N — the southernmost CNSA launch site. The low latitude adds about 460 m/s of free eastward velocity vs Jiuquan or Xichang, which is how Long March 5B can reach the 25-tonne LEO class needed to put the Tianhe core module into orbit in a single launch. Wenchang LC-101 is dedicated to Long March 5 / 5B; maiden flight November 3, 2016. It also flew Chang'e 5 (lunar sample return, 2020), Chang'e 6 (the farside sample return, 2024), and Tianwen-1 (Mars orbiter + Zhurong rover, 2020). Sister pad LC-201 next door handles Long March 7/8 manifests and achieved its first launch in June 2016.
